headline: High-risk shared-workspace interaction: Windsurf can read/write local files and use MCP, while RisingWave has no runtime isolation or egress controls documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can ingest workspace files, clipboard, and MCP content by default, so malicious content from RisingWave artifacts could be treated as instructions. RisingWave is a docs-only open-source data system with no documented isolation or provenance controls, so the pair has a plausible shared-channel injection path even though direct bridging is not explicit.
conditions: IF RisingWave-generated files are opened in Windsurf workspace files
IF an MCP server or clipboard bridge carries RisingWave output into Windsurf prompts
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based prompt ingestion in Windsurf
Keep RisingWave artifacts in a read-only folder
Require manual review before any MCP-fed content is treated as instructions
Use separate OS users for the two tools
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files and can call external model APIs, while RisingWave has no documented data-class restrictions or isolation. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, Windsurf may transmit their contents to its backend; RisingWave does not provide a documented barrier that would prevent that flow.
conditions: IF sensitive source files or secrets are present in the shared workspace
IF Windsurf sends file contents to its model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use a separate workspace for Windsurf
Turn off or restrict MCP servers
Store credentials outside project files
requires-engineering: enforce file-level DLP before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf has broad filesystem write, git modification, subprocess, and shell capabilities with shared state via local filesystem. RisingWave is not runnable here and exposes no coordination or locking surface, so any shared directory or repo can be concurrently mutated by Windsurf without a documented lock, creating direct write conflicts and git-state corruption risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local repository or workspace directory
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while RisingWave artifacts are being regenerated
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid shared git branches during concurrent use
Commit or stash before switching agents
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf can act on files and shell commands, so if it treats RisingWave outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or commands. RisingWave is a data-engineering system rather than a verifier, and no verification boundary is documented between them, so the pair supports an unverified-output-to-action chain.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes RisingWave-generated text or files as ground truth
IF auto-execute is enabled for Windsurf commands
mitigations: Require human review of RisingWave outputs before action
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Separate generation and execution steps
Annotate machine-generated files as untrusted
requires-engineering: add verification checks before command execution

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for RisingWave, while Windsurf is closed-source and may send workspace content to its model proxy. The pair therefore has a compliance gap only if regulated data is placed into Windsurf-managed files; the evidence is indirect, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files opened by Windsurf
IF Windsurf transmits those files to a third-party model proxy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Windsurf workspace
Use redacted copies for editing
Review vendor data-processing terms before use
Restrict secrets to external vaults
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
